log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: The opponent has Dragonite, Garchomp and Mimikyu, plus Volcarona and Primarina. Scarf Gholdengo threatens most of that team and can Trick its scarf onto a setup sweeper. Kingambit punishes Dragonite and Mimikyu, though it is weak to Ground. Rotom-Wash covers Volcarona and Garchomp with Levitate and Will-O-Wisp, so I lead Gholdengo, then Kingambit and Rotom-Wash in the back.

Choice Scarf Gholdengo provides an excellent offensive lead against Dragapult, Clefable, and Rotom-Wash.
Dragonite and Mimikyu offer superior defensive safety nets via Multiscale and Disguise to clean up the opposing team.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
**Analyzing Opponent's Team**

I'm focusing on the opponent's team composition, specifically the threats and pivots. I'm seeing immediate value in Choice Scarf Gholdengo, given its speed control and offensive pressure against Clefable. This addresses two of the main threats I'm observing, and leaves room to counter the remaining threats.

decisions.thought: Our Choice Scarf gives Gholdengo 223 Speed, effectively outspeeding any opposing Gholdengo (unless Scarf speed tie). Shadow Ball deals massive super-effective STAB damage for an immediate KO.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking whether that 149 Speed figure is the base stat before or after Choice Scarf, working through the level 50 stat formula for Gholdengo to see what its natural max speed would be.

Running the Shadow Ball damage calculation against likely Special Defense ranges, it looks like it should OHKO an uninvested target thanks to STAB and super-effective type coverage, so sticking with Shadow Ball makes sense even while locked in by the Scarf. I also consider switching to Kingambit for resistance purposes, but Shadow Ball remains the stronger play here.

The opposing Gholdengo outsped our scarf Gholdengo, so it's likely scarf or tied speed, and it used Shadow Ball, suggesting a possible lock-in. Kingambit resists Ghost and can hit back hard with Kowtow Cleave, getting a Supreme Overlord boost if an ally has fainted, though it's slower at 72 speed and Gholdengo could still carry Focus Blast as a threat.

decisions.thought: Gholdengo is locked into Shadow Ball, which deals negligible damage to Kingambit while Kingambit easily eliminates it. Dragonite has full HP Multiscale to comfortably take any hit and threatens Kingambit with Earthquake.

Gholdengo outspeeds Kingambit, and a Focus Blast would hit it for 4x damage. Boosted Sucker Punch moves first with priority and should knock out Gholdengo whether it attacks with Shadow Ball or Focus Blast. Kowtow Cleave would be safer against a switch, but it risks Kingambit getting knocked out first.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm checking the speed matchup against Gholdengo and whether Kingambit resists its attacks—Dark/Steel takes half from Ghost but Focus Blast could hit for 4x. Then I'm estimating Kowtow Cleave's damage output against a roughly neutral defense stat, factoring in STAB and the crit-like multiplier.

Kowtow Cleave punishes switches but risks eating a Focus Blast KO, so I'll go with Sucker Punch as the safer play.

decisions.thought: Dragonite outspeeds Kingambit and has full Multiscale intact to comfortably absorb any attack. Super-effective Earthquake will deal massive damage to Kingambit, easily putting it in range of a follow-up.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm weighing Dragonite's likely moves—Dragon Dance or Earthquake/Extreme Speed—against Kingambit's resistances, noting Extreme Speed gets resisted while Earthquake hits super effectively, and factoring in Multiscale and the possibility Kingambit sets up with Swords Dance.

Running the math, a Kowtow Cleave now would break Multiscale and deal solid damage, while Swords Dance first delays the kill since the shield stays up; attacking immediately to crack Multiscale then finishing with a second Kowtow Cleave looks like the better two-turn plan, with Sucker Punch as a backup if Dragonite goes for Dragon Dance instead.

decisions.thought: Earthquake dealt 58% last turn, putting Kingambit at 42%, which is well within KO range. Sucker Punch does not have enough power to KO Dragonite from 65.7% HP.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit's down to 89 HP while Dragonite sits at 65%; Kowtow Cleave only did 35% likely because multiscale was still active, but now it's broken so a repeat hit should do around 70% and knock Dragonite out. Still, Dragonite outspeeds and its Earthquake already hit for 118, meaning another one would finish off Kingambit first—so I need to weigh Sucker Punch's priority against that threat.

Sucker Punch alone won't finish Dragonite, and Kingambit dies to EQ next turn anyway, so Kowtow is pointless unless Dragonite doesn't attack. Switching to Rotom-Wash preserves Kingambit and lets me Will-O-Wisp to cripple Dragonite, even accounting for the Dragon Dance/Extreme Speed risk. I'll go with Rotom.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash cannot immediately threaten a knockout on Dragonite, and Lum Berry protects against Will-O-Wisp. Setting up Dragon Dance gives Dragonite the Speed and Attack boost needed to clean up both Rotom-Wash and Kingambit.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Dragonite is physical, so Will-O-Wisp cripples it by halving its attack and protecting my team, which seems better than a Volt Switch that would only do neutral damage of around 25% against it at 65% health. I'll go with Will-O-Wisp.

decisions.thought: Dragonite outspeeds Rotom-Wash at +1 Speed. At +1 Attack, Outrage deals massive damage and easily finishes off Rotom-Wash, putting the game away.

Dragonite's Lum Berry is gone, so a second Will-O-Wisp burn sticks and halves its +1 Attack. Rotom at full HP with high Defense can take one boosted hit first. Switching Kingambit in at 43% risks it being knocked out by Earthquake.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: With Dragonite boosted and moving first, I'm weighing whether Will-O-Wisp's burn would meaningfully blunt its damage output against Rotom's solid defense, since its likely coverage moves probably wouldn't OHKO anyway. I'm also considering Kingambit as an alternative answer.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is locked into Outrage. Even with burn halving physical damage, +1 Outrage will comfortably KO Rotom-Wash from 38% HP.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite is still locked into Outrage while burned, which roughly halves its damage output — if unburned Outrage did 135, burned it's likely closer to 67, which should still be enough to knock out Rotom at 61 HP.

The real question is what to switch in after Outrage ends. Kingambit resists Dragon and could tank the reduced Outrage decently given its high defense, taking it down to around 47 HP, and it also matches up well against Gholdengo with Kowtow Cleave hitting super effectively. Keeping Rotom in reserve for the Gholdengo matchup makes sense, so switching Kingambit in now seems like the better play.

decisions.thought: Dragonite is locked into Outrage, leaving it as the only legal action to finish off or heavily damage Kingambit.

decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Dragonite used Outrage on turns 6 and 7, so it's likely still locked into the move for turn 8 since no confusion message appeared yet, meaning it probably hit for a third consecutive turn dealing 161 damage.

Now with Kingambit at 46 HP, Outrage would finish it off, but Sucker Punch acts first against an attacking move — I'm estimating it does roughly 108 damage to Dragonite, which sits around 53% HP (~95), likely enough for a KO. Switching to Rotom instead carries similar risk since it'd also take a big Outrage hit, so going with Sucker Punch seems like the better play.

decisions.thought: Mimikyu has Disguise intact, making it completely immune to being KOed by Kingambit's Sucker Punch while safely finishing it off.
Mimikyu has Disguise intact to safely absorb any attack Kingambit uses. Kingambit is at 22% HP, easily in range of Life Orb boosted Play Rough.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
**Analyzing Kingambit's Actions**

I've determined that Kingambit's low HP strongly suggests a priority move, probably Sucker Punch, or a strong attack like Iron Head or Kowtow Cleave. With Mimikyu's Disguise, I'm leaning toward Play Rough; it's a good move, but Kingambit might not use Sucker Punch if I Swords Dance.

I'm weighing Kingambit's matchup against Mimikyu, checking which moves resist or hit through Disguise — Fairy and Ghost moves get resisted by Dark/Steel, but Fighting-type options like Drain Punch would be quadruple effective.

Either way, Kingambit likely can't survive long: whether I lead with Iron Head to break Disguise or Mimikyu attacks first with an unboosted Play Rough, the math suggests Kingambit falls around 46 HP, so the realistic goal is just trading it to pop the Disguise before it dies.

decisions.thought: Kingambit has fainted, so Rotom-Wash is the only Pokémon I have left. Switching it in is the only legal action.
Rotom-Wash is the opponent's last Pokémon at 38% HP and Mimikyu is faster. Life Orb Shadow Claw has 100% accuracy and will easily secure the knockout to win the match.

Rotom is my last Pokémon, and at 61 HP it probably can't survive a Life Orb Play Rough. Mimikyu takes neutral damage from my attacks, and Hydro Pump won't knock it out. Will-O-Wisp halves its physical damage if Rotom moves first, and the burn chip stacks with Life Orb recoil. That gives me the best chance to outlast it.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
With Rotom as my last mon against their Mimikyu and Gholdengo, I'm checking whether a Life Orb Play Rough from Mimikyu could threaten to knock out Rotom given its defense stat, factoring in likely max attack investment and the possibility of a prior Swords Dance boost.

Comparing options: Will-O-Wisp burns Mimikyu to blunt its damage if Rotom moves first, Pain Split could trade HP favorably given their Mimikyu's current percentage, and Hydro Pump offers decent but non-lethal damage against Mimikyu's special defense. The real problem is speed—if Mimikyu outpaces Rotom, nearly every choice loses outright unless I can burn it first, and I still have Gholdengo waiting at full health afterward, so this is looking like a tough spot regardless of which move I pick.

decisions.thought: Rotom-Wash is down to 10% HP and Mimikyu's Life Orb Shadow Sneak easily secures the knockout despite the burn.

decisions.hidden_reasoning: Rotom is our last Pokémon against a healthy Gholdengo and a burned Mimikyu at 61% HP that outsped us last turn, so we're likely going to take a hit before we can act—Shadow Claw probably finishes us off at 17 HP. Our best shot might be trying Pain Split if we somehow survive the incoming attack.

With Rotom down to 3 HP, Mimikyu's priority Shadow Sneak looks like a guaranteed kill regardless of what I do, so I'm checking if Hydro Pump could at least KO the burned Mimikyu first if it doesn't choose that move.
